text:
William Karlsson is a classic hard-luck case in our numbers. He has 6 goals and 10 points in 25 games at 17.7 minutes a night, but Vegas has scored 9.9 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him on the ice. At 5v5 his team has 54.6% of the expected goals when he plays, and still the points haven't come.

It started to turn against Dallas. He scored twice on Nov. 17 and again two nights later, his third goal in two games, as Jesse Granger of The Athletic noted. His own finishing is close to normal (6 goals on 7.4 expected), so the gap is mostly pucks his linemates haven't buried.

The context matters. He played only 14 games last season, and Evolving-Hockey's read on that small sample (212 minutes) was replacement level. In those games, Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him getting 6.7 scoring chances per 60 from the area in front of the net, 87th percentile among forwards. That's still the Karlsson who won a Cup in Vegas in 2023.

Our talent range puts his scoring rate near 1.67 points per 60, above the 1.36 he's posting.
